slides.notes:
Kompast is a workspace we built in-house. It replaces the mix of docs, ticketing and side tools the BU uses today with one product we host ourselves.
In the next 15 minutes: why we need it, what it does, where it stands, and what we're asking for. The ask is approval of a full cutover.

content.text: One self-hosted workspace for docs, project tracking, automation and AI.
文件、專案追蹤、自動化與 AI，整合在一個自建的工作空間。

slides.notes:
Four problems. Cost: we pay per seat for several overlapping tools. Fragmentation: a spec, its tickets and its roadmap live in three places. Sovereignty: our internal plans live on someone else's cloud. AI: we pay extra for the vendor's AI, and we can't use the provider ASUS already approves, such as Azure OpenAI.
(Add BU numbers here if available: seat count, annual license spend.)

content.text: Our work is spread across tools we rent, but don't control.
我們的工作分散在多個租用、卻無法掌控的工具裡。
Per-seat fees for every tool, for every person, every year. And they grow with headcount.
每個工具、每個人都要付授權費
Specs in one tool, tickets in another, roadmaps in spreadsheets. Links break and context is lost.
資訊分散、連結失效、脈絡斷裂
Product plans and internal docs sit on vendor clouds, under vendor terms, outside our infrastructure.
內部資料存放在外部廠商雲端
AI is a paid add-on on the vendor's terms. We can't bring our own model or wire in our own agents.
AI 與自動化受限於廠商

slides.notes: This is what a single feature's lifecycle touches today. Each tool has its own login, search and permission model, and nothing is linked by default.

content.text: Five tools, five logins, five permission models.
五個工具、五組帳號、五套權限。

slides.notes: Kompast pulls all of this into one product. One sign-in through our existing Microsoft Entra ID, one permission model enforced at the database, all running on infrastructure we control.

content.text: One workspace, one login, one permission model.
一個工作空間、一組帳號、一套權限。

slides.notes: All screenshots come from our seeded demo workspace, "Lumen Labs", with six personas across an English software team and a Chinese marketing team. Everything shown here is built and working today.

slides.notes: For engineering teams the workflow is familiar: backlog, sprints, board, reports. The goal is that nobody feels a downgrade from JIRA. Click to switch from the board to the backlog.

slides.notes: The docs side is Notion-like. The difference from today is that a spec and its tickets live in the same place and link to each other natively: mention an issue in a doc, or embed a live board.

content.text: Real-time docs that live next to the work.
即時協作文件，與工作項目緊密連結。
with nested pages, templates and version history

and embed live boards inside a page

slides.notes: This is a concern HR and managers raise with shared tools: personal notes like 1:1s and reviews. Private means private, even from admins. When someone leaves, their knowledge isn't lost: the super admin can recover it, and that action is audit-logged.

slides.notes: Visibility rules are enforced in Postgres, not just hidden in the UI. That matters for cross-team confidentiality, for example Finance or unreleased product plans. On the right, the Marketing team works fully in Traditional Chinese and dark mode, and can't see engineering's projects.

content.text: Each team sees its own work. The database enforces it.
各團隊只看得到自己的內容，由資料庫層強制執行。
Creates teams, appoints team admins, sees every team.
Creates projects and invites people straight into the team.
Sees only their own teams' projects, issues, sprints and docs. Other teams appear locked.

elements.alt: Marketing board in Chinese, dark mode

content.text: Postgres row-level security applies the same rules to the UI, the REST API, AI agents (MCP) and Ask Kompast. A missed check in the app can't leak another team's data.

slides.notes: This is the automation canvas on each project. Step through it: a trigger, a condition, then actions on each branch. Team leads can build these themselves. Dry-run mode and rate limits stop a bad rule from flooding people. Every run is logged per node, so it's easy to debug.

content.text: Teams automate their own workflows. No scripts needed.
視覺化流程編輯器，團隊自行打造自動化，無需寫程式。

slides.notes: AI isn't a separate subscription here. We plug in the provider ASUS already approves, such as Azure OpenAI, and data stays within that agreement. MCP is the standard protocol AI agents use to work with tools, so engineers' coding agents can file and update tickets directly. Everything an agent does is attributed as "MCP" in the activity feed.

content.text: AI, built in · 內建 AI
AI on our terms: our provider, our data.
AI 由我們掌控：自選供應商，資料不外流。
Continue, improve, summarize or translate inside any doc. AI drafts issue descriptions and sprint summaries.
Chat with our own project history. Answers come from issues and comments, scoped to what you're allowed to see.
Azure OpenAI, Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set by an admin. Usage logged per call.
: tools like Claude Code can read and update issues, sprints and docs with a personal token.

slides.notes: For IT and security reviewers: there's exactly one place where each action is implemented and permission-checked, and the database enforces tenant and team isolation underneath that. Sign-in uses our existing Entra ID. It deploys as Docker containers on infrastructure we choose.

content.text: Three ways in, one set of rules.
三種存取方式，同一套規則。
Every action is implemented once, with one permission check. The three entry points can't drift apart in what they allow.
Workspace and team isolation enforced by the database itself. It fails closed.
Sign in with ASUS accounts. No new passwords.
Docker on our infrastructure. Data never leaves.
Provider keys encrypted at rest, never sent back to the browser.
Every change tagged: person, automation, API, MCP or import.

slides.notes: The core trade: we stop renting per-seat licenses and take on running one product. The next slides cover what that ownership costs, honestly, and how we de-risk it.

content.text: Why build, not buy · 為何自建
對事業單位帶來的改變。
Our servers, our backups, our retention
Entra SSO and one permission model, team-scoped
Same workspace: native mentions and embeds
Vendor's model as a paid add-on
Set by us: built for how this BU works

slides.notes: Everything except the production hardening pass is built. Importers for the two tools we actually use, JIRA and Notion, are done. Hardening, meaning backups, monitoring and resilience work, is the remaining step before we put real data on it.

content.text: Where we are · 開發進度
The core platform is built and working.
核心平台已完成並可運作。

slides.notes: The importers are designed so we can rehearse the migration as many times as needed. Dry-run first, then real runs that can be repeated safely. Imported history doesn't spam anyone with notifications or trigger automation rules.

slides.notes: We don't flip a switch on day one. Phase 1 closes the known production gaps. Phase 2 rehearses the migration with each team lead. Phase 3 is the actual cutover, with the old tools kept read-only as a safety net. Phase 4 ends the licenses. (Add target dates per phase before presenting.)

content.text: Four phases, each gated on a clear exit criterion.
四個階段，每階段皆有明確完成標準。

slides.notes: Being upfront: these are the real gaps today, all documented in our engineering notes. The first two are blockers we close before go-live. The ownership risk is real but bounded: it's a standard stack and well documented.

content.text: Scheduled database dumps with off-box retention and a tested restore. A Phase 1 exit gate.
Mainstream stack (React, Postgres, Docker), documented engineering notes, automated test suite on real databases.
與成熟產品的功能差距
Email digests, outbound notification webhooks, AI search over docs. Prioritized from pilot feedback.

slides.notes: Three concrete approvals: the plan itself, the production infrastructure, and a named champion from each team. Once Phase 4 completes, the per-seat licenses end.

content.text: Approve a full cutover of the BU to Kompast.
同意事業單位全面切換至 Kompast。
Four-phase cutover, gated on the Phase 1 hardening exit criteria.
Server, managed Postgres and storage on ASUS-managed infrastructure.
One migration champion per team to validate imports and support colleagues.
